cadence.title: Collection cadence
cadence.blurb: How often each agent does the work. Every number here is time on somebody's machine and traffic on the wire: lower is fresher and more expensive.

history.title: Stored history
history.blurb: What is written to the database and how long it stays. This is the group that costs disk.

caps.title: Caps
caps.blurb: Upper bounds on a single answer, so one enormous repository or a runaway working tree cannot fill a response.

lists.title: Lists
lists.blurb: Where the agents look, and which coding agents they report on.

sweep.title: Host sweep
sweep.blurb: Deleting hosts that have gone silent. It is off unless you turn it on, and it is the only setting on this page that destroys anything.

access.title: Fleet-wide CLI tokens
access.blurb: A token minted on the Coding CLI access screen reaches every host in this fleet, not one machine. Host-by-host keys are unaffected.

heartbeatSec.label: Heartbeat interval (seconds)
heartbeatSec.why: How often every agent reports in. Nothing a card shows can be fresher than this, and every host pays it on the wire — the cheapest thing the fleet does, and the most frequent.

gitIntervalSec.label: Git collection interval (seconds)
gitIntervalSec.why: How often an agent re-reads the checkouts it found. Walking repositories costs far more than a heartbeat, so this is measured in minutes.

usageIntervalSec.label: Coding-agent usage interval (seconds)
usageIntervalSec.why: How often an agent re-reads the usage windows of the providers below. Far costlier than a heartbeat: it reads each provider's own state, not a counter.

probeTimeoutMs.label: Service probe timeout (ms)
probeTimeoutMs.why: How long one service probe may hang before it is called down. A cap, not a target — without it a single unresponsive port would hold up the whole heartbeat behind it.

metricStepSec.label: Metric sample interval (seconds)
metricStepSec.why: How far apart stored CPU, memory and disk samples are. Heartbeats arrive every few seconds, and storing each one would write about 17,000 rows per host per day to draw a graph whose pixels are 30 seconds apart.

metricRetentionDays.label: Metric history kept (days)
metricRetentionDays.why: How long stored samples live before the prune job deletes them. This is the number that decides how much disk the fleet's history costs.

gitLimit.label: Commits per repository
gitLimit.why: How many commits the graph window holds for one repository. Past it the graph says it is truncated rather than growing without limit.

gitDetailBudget.label: New commit details per pass
gitDetailBudget.why: How many previously unseen commit bodies and patches an agent may collect in one pass. It is what stops a freshly registered repository from sending its entire history at once.

statusFileCap.label: Changed files per repository
statusFileCap.why: How many working-tree entries are reported for one repository. A tree with thousands of untracked files would otherwise become the largest thing on the wire.

bodyMaxChars.label: Commit message body (characters)
bodyMaxChars.why: How much of a commit message body is stored. Long enough for a real message, short enough that a pasted log is not kept forever.

terminalBufferBytes.label: Terminal buffer per pane (bytes)
terminalBufferBytes.why: How much output an agent holds for one pane before the oldest bytes are dropped. The relay uses the same number toward the browser, so raising it costs memory in two places.

gitRoots.label: Git roots
gitRoots.why: Directories each agent scans for checkouts. These are paths on the hosts, not on this server; empty means nothing is collected. A host with its own paths ignores this list.

usageProviders.label: Coding-agent providers
usageProviders.why: Which providers' usage windows the agents report — the rows on a card's coding-agent widget. A name nobody runs simply reports nothing.

staleHostRetentionDays.label: Delete a host after (days of silence)
staleHostRetentionDays.why: 0 turns this off, and off is how it ships. Any other number lets the server DELETE a host that has not reported in for that long, taking its agent tokens, enrollment codes, services and collected history with it. That machine is then refused until somebody registers it again and re-runs the installer.

mcpUserTokens.label: Allow fleet-wide tokens
mcpUserTokens.hint: Off by default. Turning it off does NOT revoke anything: existing tokens stop working immediately and start again if it is turned back on.

sweep.offNote: 0 — no host is ever deleted automatically. This is the shipped default.
sweep.onNote: On. Hosts silent for longer than the window are deleted on the next sweep, and the list warns for the last seven days before that.
sweep.neverSwept: A host that has never connected is never swept: a row with no last-seen is a machine whose installer has not run yet.
sweep.armWarning: Every host silent for longer than the window is DELETED on the next sweep, with its agent tokens, enrollment codes, services and collected history. Each of those machines is then refused until somebody registers it again and re-runs the installer. This cannot be undone.
sweep.atRisk: {count} hosts are already past {days} days and would go on the next sweep:
sweep.atRiskNone: No host is past {days} days today, so the next sweep would take nothing — but any host that goes quiet for that long afterwards will.
